SameStoryVerdict.description:
The three words a judge may answer with, and nothing else.

Upper case on the wire deliberately. The grammar handed to the decoder emits
these spellings, and the three differ at the first generated token - which is
what makes `first_token_margin` a reading about this pair rather than about
where the three words happen to agree.
SameStoryVerdict.title: SameStoryVerdict

changelog.change: Initial shape: one pair, two readings, and the scorer and judge behind them.
changelog.why: The merge line was one person's reading, and nothing recorded what it cost.

description: One pair, what it scored, and what a judge said about it in both orders.

composite_score.description: The weighted score the same-story pass would have given this pair. This is the number the fitted line is compared against, and the judge never sees it.
composite_score.title: Composite Score

cosine.description: The cosine between the two vectors the day already carries. Recorded raw so a later reweighting can be computed from the row rather than re-run.
cosine.title: Cosine

cosine_weight.description: What the cosine was worth when this row was scored, read from the committed config at scoring time. On the row rather than in a file a reader has to go and find, so a window spanning a config edit is still readable.
cosine_weight.title: Cosine Weight

date.description: The digest date whose items this pair came from.
date.title: Date

decode_seconds.description: Wall clock for both calls on this pair. A per-pair reading, so a day's spread is readable off the day file; the leg bound is sized off its own run instead.
decode_seconds.title: Decode Seconds

first_token_margin.description: The gap between the highest and the second-highest probability at the first generated position, on the file-order call. A margin near zero means the grammar chose and the model did not.
first_token_margin.title: First Token Margin

grammar_digest.description: sha256 of the grammar handed to the decoder. A grammar edit changes what the three words can be, so it is part of what the verdict means.
grammar_digest.title: Grammar Digest

headline.description: Whether the two items shared a headline, which makes the score 1.0 outright instead of the weighted sum. On the row because the two paths give one number by two rules, and a reader cannot tell them apart afterwards.
headline.title: Headline

judge_model.description: Which model judged. A Literal for the same reason the scorer is one.
judge_model.title: Judge Model

key_point.description: The share of key-point words the two items have in common, on the same 0 to 1 scale. Recorded raw for the same reason as the cosine.
key_point.title: Key Point

key_point_weight.description: What the key-point term was worth. Same reason as the cosine weight.
key_point_weight.title: Key Point Weight

left_url_key.description: The lower of the two address keys. Not an item id: an id is minted per day and this pair has to be recognisable across days.
left_url_key.title: Left Url Key

pair_key.description: The pair's identity: sha256 of the two url keys joined in sorted order. Recomputed on read, never trusted from the row.
pair_key.title: Pair Key

prompt_digest.description: sha256 of the rendered system turn. The prompt is content, so a digest is the only honest shape for it.
prompt_digest.title: Prompt Digest

right_url_key.description: The higher of the two address keys. Sorted so one pair has one row rather than two.
right_url_key.title: Right Url Key

run_id.description: The run that scored the pair. Two runs of one day judge the same pair twice, and both rows stay: each read its own day.
run_id.title: Run Id

scorer_model.description: Which encoder produced the two vectors. A Literal rather than a string, so swapping the encoder is a schema diff and a changelog entry rather than a silent change of scale.
scorer_model.title: Scorer Model

shard.description: Which judging leg owns this row. index mod shards, never a contiguous block, so a truncated draw still spreads evenly across the legs.
shard.title: Shard

usable.description: Whether the two readings agree. Only an agreed pair is folded into the record; a disagreement is a reading about the judge rather than about the pair.
usable.title: Usable

verdict.description: What the judge said with the items in file order. Empty until a judging leg has read the pair.

verdict_swapped.description: What the judge said with the same two items in the other order. Two readings of one pair, which is what makes disagreement measurable.

title: StorySimilarityPair
